newsitem.title: USA: Hilton has no plans to change ITT bid now. [CORRECTED 02:00 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Hilton has no plans to change ITT bid now. [CORRECTED 02:00 GMT]

text.p: Hilton Hotels Corp on Thursday said it had no immediate plans to change its bid for ITT Corp in light of ITT's decision to sell its 50 percent stake in Madison Square Garden sports and entertainment properties.
"Our bid is still our bid," Hilton spokesman Marc Grossman said. "There's no immediate plan to change our bid."
Earlier, ITT said it planned to sell its stake in MSG to Cablevision Systems Corp for $650 million.
(Corrects from "...will sell its stake in Cablevision...")
Grossman said Hilton would need to study the financial terms of the deal before making a decision.
In a statement, Hilton President Stephen Bollenbach said his company was pleased that ITT had decided to sell non-core assets such as MSG.

"We are pleased that ITT appears to be executing the strategy we first endorsed in January of selling non-core assets," Bollenbach said. "This move by ITT makes the ultimate job of selling non-strategic assets that much easier, enhances our interest in the company and strengthens our resolve to make this combination a reality."
"We hope that ITT's management will now let the shareholders vote on the matter at their regularly scheduled May annual meeting," Bollenbach added.

Hilton offered to acquire ITT in January for a combination of cash and stock worth $6.5 billion. Hilton also offered to assume $4.0 billion in debt, bringing the total value of the deal to $10.5 billion.
ITT rejected the bid and embarked on a program to shed non-core assets in an effort to raise cash and perhaps offer shareholders a special dividend.

Separately, Hilton said a U.S. District Court Judge in Nevada declined to grant Hilton's motions seeking to prevent ITT from increasing the size of its board or interfering with the board election process.

In making the decision, the court said it could not rule in Hilton's favor because ITT had not done anything yet to affect the board election process. Hilton said the court did allow the company to file for an injunction later on if it believed ITT was trying to disrupt the process.
In a statement, Hilton said ITT had represented to the court that it did not intend to increase the size of its board.
ITT said it was pleased with the court ruling.

"It represents the spirit and letter of the law," an ITT spokesman said. "We are satisfied that the merits of our position were upheld in this case, especially since we have not attempted to change our bylaws, nor have we increased the number of our directors."
